clue.text: Very tiny boat with a man in charge

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a kind of boat
Tom is a man's name, and a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A tiny boat with one man as its skipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word joining SUB to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Particles smaller than an atom are as tiny as matter gets, so the adjective fits 'very tiny'.

clue.text: Parking so men can get round track

indicators.note: the outer words getting round means they surround the parking letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Parking arranged so soldiers can get round a track.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail or droppings left by an animal, which hunters follow as a track.

clue.text: Second-hand medal going first at a loss

indicators.note: the medal is said to go in front of the other piece

parts.note: BEM is the British Empire Medal
second-hand goods are used

explanation.surface: A second-hand medal being the first thing sold when broke.
explanation.walkthrough: The British Empire Medal is a UK honour for civil or military service.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused means puzzled or bewildered, as is someone who is at a loss.

clue.text: Beer down under is thin and metallic

definitions.meaning: in Australian slang a can of beer
describing a sound that is weak and ... like tin

explanation.surface: Australian beer criticised for its thin, metallic taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians call a can of beer by this name, and a cheap tin-like sound is described with the same word.

clue.text: Where astronaut may one day get wine and chocolate?

definitions.text: Where astronaut may one day get wine
definitions.meaning: a bar on the planet Mars, where a future astronaut might buy a drink
a popular British chocolate bar with nougat and caramel

explanation.surface: Planning a space traveller's future treat of wine and chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known confectionery is named after a planet, and a drinking spot on that planet would share the name.

clue.text: Carried on to make flavouring

indicators.note: the letters are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone continued in order to produce a flavouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriander is a herb whose leaves and seeds are used to flavour food.

clue.text: Ordered Powell to stop short

indicators.note: stopping short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: Baden is the word paired with Powell in Baden-Powell, founder of the Scout movement

explanation.surface: Someone ordered a person called Powell to halt before going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Baden-Powell founded the Scouts; 'Powell' calls up its partner BADEN, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bade is the past tense of bid, as in 'bid him come', meaning commanded.

clue.text: Mixer (large) swallowed in drinking bout

indicators.note: being swallowed in something puts the letter inside it

parts.note: a bender is a heavy drinking spree
L is the abbreviation for large on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A large mixer drink downed during a heavy session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixer' looks like a drink such as tonic; it is the kitchen appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A blender is a kitchen appliance that mixes and purees food.

clue.text: Religious lecturer securing taxi to drop book off

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly inside

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so the book letter is taken away
off reinforces that the book letter is removed from the taxi

parts.note: a minicab is a hired car, a kind of taxi

explanation.surface: A religious lecturer keeping a taxi waiting while a book is dropped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' and 'off' together signal the book letter's removal; 'securing' puts the shortened taxi inside the lecturer. A minicab is a British private-hire car booked ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dominican is a member of the Order of Preachers, a religious order of friars.

clue.text: Haircut on kid is one way to ring the changes

definitions.text: one way to ring the changes

parts.note: a bob is a short, even haircut
a minor is a child, someone under age

explanation.surface: A short haircut on a child as a way of trying something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word. Change ringing is the English art of ringing church bells in set sequences called methods.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Minor is a standard change-ringing method on six bells, so it is literally one way of ringing changes.

clue.text: City boundaries gas penetrates

indicators.note: penetrating means pushing inside, so the gas goes into the boundaries

parts.note: rims are edges or boundaries
He is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas

explanation.surface: Gas seeping across a city's borders.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheims, also spelt Reims, is a cathedral city in the Champagne region of France.

clue.text: Lively end to working week, heaven

parts.note: Fri, short for Friday, is the last day of the working week
the sky is the heavens above

explanation.surface: Friday arrives and the end of the working week feels like heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky describes someone playful and full of energy, a close synonym of lively.

clue.text: Getting on at this school?

definitions.meaning: climbing aboard a bus, train or plane
pupils who live in at their school are at a ... school

explanation.definitionFit: Boarding is the act of going aboard transport, and also the word for a school where pupils live in.

clue.text: Believe journalist struck through review

indicators.note: something struck through another runs inside it, so the journalist sits within the review

parts.note: a crit is a critique or review
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist's piece crossed out by a critic, hard to believe.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to accept it as true, a synonym of believe.

clue.text: Perform in terror, twanging muscle

indicators.note: in places the performing letters inside the other group
twanging like a plucked string, the letters are jangled out of order

parts.note: to act is to perform

explanation.surface: Performing while terrified, with a muscle twanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twanging' rearranges the six letters of 'terror' to RETROR, and 'in' splits them after the fourth letter to take the performing word.
explanation.definitionFit: A retractor is a muscle that draws a body part back, such as the eyeball retractor.

clue.text: In US, smart retreat by black political leader

parts.note: in American slang tony means stylish or upmarket
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
a lair is a den or hideaway, a retreat

explanation.surface: A political leader in the US with a smart hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word putting LAIR beside B.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair led the UK Labour Party and was Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007.

clue.text: Right-wing, unreliable person not found at such a university?

definitions.text: Right-wing, unreliable person not found at such a university?

parts.words: Right-wing, unreliable person not found at such a university?
parts.note: a red is a left-winger and a brick is a reliable person, so a right-wing unreliable type is the opposite of this kind of university

explanation.surface: A snobbish remark that untrustworthy Tories avoid certain universities.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'a brick' is a dependable person and 'a red' a leftist; redbrick universities are the civic ones founded in Victorian industrial cities.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue describes the opposite of a reliable leftist, and that pairing names the British civic university type.

clue.text: Dwarfs stay extremely desirable, they learn

indicators.note: the dwarfs stay around the letters, holding them in place inside

parts.note: to dwarf something is to stunt its growth

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters of the word desirable

explanation.surface: Little people staying on, which is highly desirable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dwarfs' looks like a plural noun but is the verb, giving STUNTS, which holds DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils at college or university are people whose job is learning.

clue.text: Research for one that is not worth explaining

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a ..., which is an example of an academic's work
the reply given when an explanation would be too long or painful

explanation.definitionFit: Research is a typical academic's job, so splitting the answer gives a lecturer's duty; as a phrase it waves away a question.

clue.text: He yawns uncontrollably: should I stop?

indicators.note: letters out of control fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A man yawns without restraint while being served a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what someone pouring a drink says, asking when to stop pouring.

clue.text: The turf green for this British activity

definitions.text: The turf green for this British activity

parts.words: The turf green for this British activity
parts.note: the turf is horse ..., and British ... green is the classic colour of British motor-... cars

explanation.surface: A green lawn laid down for a British pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: British racing green is the dark green once used on British cars in international motor racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse racing is known as the turf, and the colour phrase completes with this word.

clue.text: Conservative barrister, not old, is to screw up

indicators.note: not old says the letter for old is removed

parts.note: Rumpole of the Bailey is a famous fictional London barrister

explanation.surface: A Tory barrister, no longer old, about to make a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to' links the definition. O is the abbreviation for old.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw up a sheet of paper is to scrunch it into a ball, a synonym for that crushing action.

clue.text: Ballad from north anybody plays

indicators.note: the letters play about, moving freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A song from the north that anyone can play.
explanation.definitionFit: Danny Boy is a famous sentimental Irish song sung to the Londonderry Air, a classic ballad.

clue.text: Work units heard of in Holland

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken, so a name that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: Jools Holland is a British pianist and TV music presenter, so his first name is the one coming before Holland

explanation.surface: Units of work that people have heard of in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holland' seems to be the country; it is Jools Holland, host of the BBC music show Later.
explanation.definitionFit: The joule is the SI unit of energy and of work done, named after physicist James Joule.

clue.text: Lucky to get stuck on yacht

parts.note: to jam is to become stuck fast
MY is the prefix for motor yacht

explanation.surface: Lucky to be stranded aboard a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'on' are link words. Jammy is British slang for lucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Jammy is informal British English for fortunate, often with a hint of undeserved luck.

clue.text: Birdie? Yes and no

parts.note: the creature is a bird, yes, but in golf this score is two under par, not a birdie, which is one under

explanation.surface: A hesitant answer to whether something counts as a little bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The raptor is certainly a bird, yet on a golf card it is a better score than a birdie, so the answer is both.

clue.text: A pastry's turned into layers

indicators.note: turned means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a tart is a pastry, and the possessive adds the S

explanation.surface: A pastry turned out in layers, like puff pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are the layers of rock or of society, plural of stratum.

clue.text: Google's house servant

parts.note: a home is a house
a page is a young servant or attendant

explanation.surface: Google employs a domestic servant at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Google's' as 'Google is': the search engine's front page is many people's starting web page.
explanation.definitionFit: Google's search page is the starting page many browsers open, so Google stands for this kind of page.

clue.text: Strong drink some fear a killer

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A potent drink that some people dread as a killer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arak is an aniseed-flavoured spirit from the Middle East, a strong alcoholic liquor.

clue.text: Place for charter party not set: Imogen finally picked venue

parts.note: a runny jelly or egg has not set firm
Imogen is the setter, who refers to themself as me

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the two words after it

explanation.surface: The party venue the setter chose because the jelly would not set.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often name themselves for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Magna Carta was sealed at Runnymede by the Thames in 1215, the meadow where the charter's parties met.
